title: Achu soup (Cameroonian yellow soup with pounded cocoyam)

ingredients.name: beef, cut in chunks (a little tripe or cow skin is traditional)
kanwa (food-grade potash), or 1/2 tsp baking soda as a substitute
ground njansang or ground pumpkin seeds (optional)

steps: Simmer the beef in the water with the garlic, half the pepper and the stock cube for about 1 hour until tender. Keep the broth.
Boil the taro in plenty of water for 30 to 40 minutes until very soft.
Drain the taro and pound or mash it with a heavy pestle or potato masher, adding a splash of hot water until you have a smooth, stretchy dough. Shape into balls and keep warm.
Dissolve the kanwa (or baking soda) in 3 tablespoons of warm water, let it settle and keep only the clear liquid.
Put the palm oil in a bowl and slowly beat in the clear liquid, a little at a time, until the oil turns thick, pale yellow and creamy.
Stir the yellow emulsion into the hot beef broth along with the chilli and ground seeds, and simmer for 5 minutes. Do not boil hard or it may split.
Serve the soup over the taro dough in wide bowls, with the beef on top.

title: Koki (Cameroonian steamed black-eyed pea pudding)

ingredients.name: ground crayfish or 1 tsp mushroom powder (optional)
banana leaves or foil, for wrapping
ripe or green plantains, to serve

steps: Soak the peas overnight in plenty of cold water, then rub them between your hands to loosen and rinse off the skins; drain.
Blend the peeled peas with the onion, chilli, salt and just enough cold water to make a thick, fluffy paste; it should hold a spoon upright.
Beat in the palm oil until evenly coloured.
Cut banana leaves into rectangles, soften over a flame or in hot water, and spoon about 1/2 cup of paste in the centre of each. Fold into tight parcels, or use foil.
Steam the parcels in a pot with a rack and a little water for 60 to 75 minutes until firm.
Boil or fry the plantains and serve them beside the unwrapped koki.

title: Kondreh (Cameroonian goat and green plantain stew)

ingredients.name: goat meat on the bone, cut in pieces (or lamb)
green (unripe) plantains, peeled and cut in chunks
scotch bonnet or other hot chilli, left whole

steps: Put the goat in a large heavy pot with the water, onion, garlic, thyme, bay leaves, salt and black pepper. Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer for 45 minutes.
Stir in the palm oil, tomato, nutmeg and whole chilli and continue cooking for 20 minutes.
Add the plantain pieces on top of the meat, pushing them down into the broth.
Cover and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until the plantains are soft and the meat is tender; add a little water if the pot starts to dry.
Press a few plantain pieces against the side of the pot to thicken the sauce, remove the chilli and bay leaves, and taste for seasoning.
Serve hot, directly from the pot.
